title: Cross-cutting obligations are restated in every finance domain file
description: 127 of 342 slice-A requirements (37%) [D: count of register rows with disposition consolidate] restate an obligation that already has a canonical owner: append-only/correction (≥10 copies), tenant isolation (9), API governance (8), Forma accessibility (8), Folio documents (7), Strata (6). Each copy uses different attribute lists, so implementers and testers cannot tell which text governs.
impact: Inconsistent implementation, duplicated test traces and review effort; any change must be made in up to ten places.
proposed_resolution: Adopt the survivor map in report section "Duplicate and consolidation clusters"; domain files keep only domain-specific clauses and cite the survivor ID.

title: Strata ledger guarantees still normative in five domain files
description: RCD-027 and RR-UNB-ACC-026-r1 limit Strata to schema governance and put ledger guarantees on PostgreSQL, but the domain texts still assign append-only, replay and integrity guarantees to Strata.
impact: Implementers may wait on, or build against, capabilities the technology does not provide.
proposed_resolution: Consolidate all six into RR-UNB-ACC-026-r1.

title: Baseline text still requires human review of every item where decisions already adopted exception-driven control
description: RCD-035 (in-tolerance NAV published by policy), RCD-020/RCD-037 (auto-pass reconciliation with sampled attestation) and RCD-017 (pool cash buffer instead of per-grant liquidation) are decided, but UNB-NAV-008, UNB-NAV-005, UNB-GFUND-011, UNB-ACC-017 (checklists) and UNB-ACC-022 (per-journal SoD) still read as per-item human work. Estimated avoidable effort ~1,125 h per 10k accounts per year [A] across these five rows [D: sum of register avoidable hours for NAV-008 210, GFUND-011 540, ACC-017 170, ACC-022 175, GFUND-012 30].
impact: If implemented literally, these texts add roughly a quarter of the expected-case grant-exception workload (4,800 h per 10k accounts [D]) back into finance operations.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-NAV-008-r1, RR-UNB-NAV-005-r1, RR-UNB-GFUND-011-r1, RR-UNB-ACC-017-r1 and RR-UNB-ACC-022-r1. Every control stays; only its trigger moves from every item to exceptions, samples and rule versions.

title: Adopted refinement keeps native budgeting that the same discovery rejected
description: RR-UNB-ACC-014-r1 (adopted) begins "Support budgeting, forecasts, actual-versus-budget reporting, cost centers and scenario models", while XRJ-ERP-002 rejects native budgeting/forecasting.
impact: Builders may implement a budgeting module that duplicates the sponsor FP&A tool.
proposed_resolution: Issue RR-UNB-ACC-014-r2 keeping only the non-posting boundary and import of budgets for comparison.

title: Operating-ERP scope remains normative in FULL-ACCOUNTING-SYSTEM.md
description: RCF-FIN-008 proposed native DAF books plus summarized export, with AP, AR, budgeting, payroll, fixed assets and consolidation excluded; only UNB-ACC-012 was refined. Nine sibling requirements still mandate ERP functions.
impact: A second operating-finance system to build, configure (~150 chart settings [A]) and reconcile against the sponsor ERP. Note: the AP/payroll labour itself does not disappear; it stays in the sponsor ERP (moving work is not elimination).
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-ACC-004-r1 and RR-UNB-ACC-014-r2; defer UNB-ACC-013/-015; condition UNB-ACC-016; scope UNB-ACC-019 by book of record (SPD-FIN-002).

title: Percentage-grant and multi-source funding options exceed the release-1 investment structure
description: Five percentage bases, independent funding weights, donor templates and recurring percentages assume multi-portfolio funds. Release 1 has one pool or a cash sweep, so these options add donor decisions and dispute cases without enabling anything.
impact: Donor friction (more fields and concepts per grant), ~25 settings [A], and test surface.
proposed_resolution: R1: FixedAmount plus Percentage of available-to-recommend, fixed at approval; default cash-first waterfall; defer the rest (SPD-FIN-001).

title: Investment-structure optionality is the largest latent per-account cost driver
description: Per-DAF segregated custody accounts, multiple custodians, SMAs, native rebalancing/pre-trade compliance and per-fund TWR/MWR (stated three times) duplicate custodian/manager functions. Per-DAF custody accounts turn sponsor-level work (opening, reconciliation) into per-account work (~0.5 h opening per account [A]).
impact: If enabled without a fee that covers it, per-account cost rises in exactly the segment XIF-ADV-001 shows is unprofitable.
proposed_resolution: Keep as conditional capability profiles; remove UNB-INV-031 (SPD-FIN-005); one performance requirement deferred; per-DAF custody only with a priced service tier.

title: Fee-engine complexity is a consequence of the asset-based fee model
description: Daily FeeBase computation, segmentation at lifecycle events, accrual-aware capacity and the chunked batch (needed because a single-transaction batch stalled approvals, report 18 B1) all follow from basis-point pricing. That is a business-model choice, not a legal requirement.
impact: Ongoing engineering and test cost; the requirements are correct given the model.
proposed_resolution: No change to requirements; record as fee-model-dependency for the economics group when comparing flat or subscription pricing.

title: Reconciliation mission created new requirements that duplicate its own refinements
description: Five UNB-RCN-FIN records restate, nearly verbatim, five RR refinements issued in the same mission (FeeBase, balancing segments, attribution method, funding states, transactional capacity).
impact: Two P0 texts per rule; divergence on later edits.
proposed_resolution: Consolidate each UNB-RCN-FIN record into its RR refinement; move the liquidity-advance clause of UNB-RCN-FIN-008 into RR-UNB-CUST-015-r1.

title: Economics measurement must not create new human work
description: The economics stack (30 rows in this slice) is cut to 10 in R1 by report 17, but UNB-XIN-ERP-006 and UNB-XIN-ECO-006 can be read as staff tagging effort categories and maintaining time equations (~160 h per 10k accounts [A]). Counter-metric floors (UNB-XIN-ECO-016) must ship with any cost loop and must not be cut with it.
impact: Measurement overhead offsets the savings it is meant to find.
proposed_resolution: Derive work-item metadata automatically (proposed revision of UNB-XIN-ERP-006); keep ECO-016 bound to ECO-015.

title: Finance configuration load needs platform default packs
description: Slice-A requirements imply ~940 sponsor settings as written [D: sum of register configuration estimates, see Slice summary]; the largest are the chart of accounts, structure eligibility, investment policy, pricing hierarchy, reconciliation thresholds and delegation of authority.
impact: Sponsor onboarding infeasible without defaults (XIF-ADV-004).
proposed_resolution: Extend XID-ADV-010 default packs to: default DAF chart, pricing hierarchy, reconciliation thresholds, DoA template, completed-gift table, investment policy skeleton, NAV materiality; sponsors may only tighten.

title: Phone-first mandate for staff accounting workbenches exceeds the accessibility obligation
description: UNB-ACC-024 requires complex accounting tasks to remain possible on a phone. WCAG 2.2 AA (UNB-PLAT-005) requires reflow, not phone-first design of reconciliation and close workbenches.
impact: Extra design and test cost for rarely used staff flows.
proposed_resolution: Keep WCAG 2.2 AA including reflow for every surface; drop the phone-first design mandate for staff accounting workbenches (SPD-FIN-006).

title: Reference per-account cost figure: model shows $272, not ~$258
description: The economic model's high-case arithmetic is "272 − 50 + 546 ≈ $768 per account" (economic-model.md l.43), implying a $272 per-account baseline [S per that line]. No $258 figure appears in economic-model.md (grep executed; no match). All dollar figures there are assumption-driven; none is measured.
impact: Any savings expressed against "$258" rests on an unverified number.
proposed_resolution: Consolidated into SPF-ECN-001 (duplicate $258 finding; SPF-ADV-017). Integrator should cite $272 (assumption-driven) or locate the $258 source.

title: Charity diligence has no defined tiers, so the default implementation is per-grant review
description: UNB-GRT-003 requires proportionate diligence but no requirement states that passing grants need no human diligence. Literal reading with the 28-31% 'needs review' proxy implies ~4,000 h per 10k accounts per year [D].
impact: ~$222k per 10k accounts per year [D at $55.45/h] of avoidable labour; donor-visible delays.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-GRT-003-r1.

title: Monitoring routes immaterial changes (leadership, filings) to human review
description: Without a materiality classification, continuous monitoring becomes continuous manual review (~3,125 h per 10k accounts [D]).
impact: Largest avoidable monitoring cost; alert fatigue risks missing material events.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-EXT-028-r1 with a counsel-approved MaterialityTable.

title: Standing human queue for stale attestations recreates manual revalidation
description: Stale evidence should be refreshed automatically; humans only on refresh failure or ambiguity.
impact: ~132 h per 10k accounts [D] and a recurring queue type.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-CHAR-013-r1.

title: Vetting economics: routine verification is already cheap in industry; savings come from reuse, materiality and exception routing, not from more AI
description: Industry pools: routine eligibility $0.14 per grant (P06 'should not exist per grant'); non-standard diligence $1.25 per grant (P07). The baseline requirements read literally imply ~10,700 h of vetting labour per 10k accounts [D], ~5x the industry-pool equivalent (~$111k [D]). A reuse/auto-renew/exception design leaves ~770 h [D].
impact: Prevents building a review-heavy vetting operation; directs AI spend to the non-standard residual only (AIE:127).
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-REQ-X-007-r2, RR-UNB-GRT-003-r1, RR-UNB-EXT-028-r1, RR-UNB-EXT-004-r2; measure via UNB-XIN-ECO-007 'cost per charity verification (new vs reuse)'.

title: Sanctions rescreening at four trigger points without disposition reuse multiplies false-positive review
description: RR-UNB-EXT-004-r1 is correct to screen at onboarding, approval, release and list updates, but silent on reuse of human false-positive dispositions; ~2,000 h per 10k accounts [D] if re-adjudicated each time.
impact: Large avoidable compliance workload; risk of rubber-stamping under volume.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-UNB-EXT-004-r2 (counsel review, SPD-GRT-003).

title: Charity knowledge requirements are stated three to four times across KNOW, EXT, CHAR and RULE
description: 80 of 370 slice rows are consolidation candidates; the largest cluster is the charity knowledge/registry/acquisition/rules set.
impact: Divergent restatements produce inconsistent implementations and inflate test and traceability cost.
proposed_resolution: Keep CHAR (registry), EXT (sources), RULE (eligibility) as canonical; convert KNOW rows to architecture references.

title: Deep-review expiry holds new approvals but renewal is not specified as automatic
description: RR-REQ-X-007-r1: 'An expired deep review MUST hold new approvals'. If renewal is manual or fails silently, donor-visible holds follow on day 181.
impact: Donor friction and staff surge at expiry boundaries.
proposed_resolution: Adopt RR-REQ-X-007-r2 (auto-renew with lead time and load spreading).

title: Checks drive positive pay, outreach, stale-dating and escheat workload
description: Check-related requirements are correct but their workload scales with check share; ACH-first policy removes most of it.
impact: ~225 h per 10k accounts [D] plus fraud exposure.
proposed_resolution: SPD-GRT-004 ACH-first default.

title: UNB-REM rows are gap placeholders now satisfied by detailed requirements
description: Counting them as active requirements inflates the register.
impact: Traceability noise.
proposed_resolution: Mark as satisfied-by references.

title: Supporting-org certification and fiscal-sponsorship evidence collected per grant rather than reused
description: Both are per-relationship facts; per-grant collection costs ~800 h per 10k accounts [D] and repeats donor/charity requests.
impact: Friction and staff time.
proposed_resolution: Capture inline and reuse per (fund, org) / (fiscal sponsor, project).

title: No measured exception incidence or minutes for vetting
description: All hour estimates rest on sourced proxies (coverage, review-need share) and assumptions; no time study exists.
impact: Savings could be over- or under-stated by multiples.
proposed_resolution: Run the 90-day time study (AIE:187) in a pilot; instrument UNB-GEX-023 metrics from day one.

title: Implementation choices stated as requirements (knowledge compiler, F# rule AST, knowledge graph)
description: No outcome depends on these forms.
impact: Constrains design without benefit.
proposed_resolution: Restate as outcomes (versioned, replayable rules; evidence-linked history).

title: Four overlapping control catalogs plus mirrored requirement files and three crosswalks
description: Control content lives in UNB-CTRL (90 rows: 30 domains x the same three objectives, 60 "per consequential event", 30 "per review period and exception" — executed by script count), UNB-SCTRL (46 executable controls), CTL (54) and TVCTL (14). OPS-001..032 and AIN-001..036 are mirrored in CSV files. Three hand-maintained crosswalks exist (494 + 1,893 + 30 rows). Seven requirements in this slice restate the control-record schema.
impact: Every catalog needs owners, attestation, mapping and drift reconciliation; templated UNB-CTRL rows are not executable controls, so attesting them is pure overhead.
proposed_resolution: One register (MON-001) with merged executable controls; generated crosswalk (SOC2-035); CSV mirrors generated from the markdown or removed.

title: Periodic owner attestation and human zero-activity sign-off duplicate continuous monitoring
description: The baseline already specifies deterministic continuous evaluation (MON-005) and by-product evidence (SOC2-004), yet SOC2-024 requires periodic owner attestation for every control and MON-002 implies zero-activity attestation. For machine-evaluated controls these signatures add no information.
impact: ~360 h/yr [D] attestation (90 controls x 4 x 1 h) and ~60 h/yr [D] zero-activity sign-off at the R1 sponsor; ~320 h/yr [D] avoidable.
proposed_resolution: RR-SOC2-024-r1 and RR-MON-002-r1: continuous evaluation, exception-driven owner action, periodic attestation only for manual controls, quarterly independent coverage review.

title: SOC 2 report scope undecided for a single-sponsor release 1
description: SOC 2 reports serve user entities; release 1 has one sponsor and no partners. The SOC2 system-description, CUEC/CSOC and audit-period requirements and internal sampling-plan testing assume a report.
impact: ~200 h/yr [A] of report-specific work plus auditor fees may be unnecessary in R1; evidence engineering remains useful regardless.
proposed_resolution: Decide per SPD-PLT-001; mark report-specific requirements conditional.

title: Human review triggered by AI involvement rather than by decision class
description: Several requirements add human sign-off, impact review, discrepancy review or an oversight screen because AI is involved. RR-AIN-003-r1 and the UNB-RCN-PLT-005 authority matrix already place humans on A3-A5 decisions; AI involvement in A0-A2 drafts, summaries and flags does not change the risk.
impact: ~220 h/yr [A] avoidable (sign-off ~100, change review ~72, conflict review ~23, seeded cases ~8, plus no standing oversight role); risk of rubber-stamp review diluting attention on reserved decisions.
proposed_resolution: RR-UNB-AI-STD-002-r1, RR-AIN-027-r1; consolidate UNB-AIO-002 into RR-AIN-003-r1; merge UX-S11 into UX-S05.

title: Three authority vocabularies (D/P/H, A0-A5, ad hoc "material/ambiguous") and two authority registries
description: UNB-CTL-001 D/P/H, UNB-RCN-PLT-005 A0-A5 and GOV-AUTH-001 authority registry describe the same mapping; UNB-RCN-PLT-005 already requires other vocabularies to reference it.
impact: Inconsistent routing; duplicated sponsor configuration (~30 + 25 settings [A]).
proposed_resolution: Single matrix/registry; D/P/H becomes a derived attribute.

title: Annual recertification with auto-suspension of delegated customer roles moves work to donors
description: Workforce-grade recertification is applied to advisors and viewers, with suspension 14 days after due date. AUTH-I2 already ends delegated rights when parent authority ends.
impact: ~0.3 donor interactions/account/yr [A]; ~75 h/yr [A] staff handling lockouts.
proposed_resolution: Event-driven expiry plus annual no-action notice (register proposed_revision; SPD-PLT-002).

title: Two-person kill-switch activation delays containment
description: Activation only moves toward a safe state (UNB-XIN-SAS-002); requiring a second person to stop harm at 02:00 delays containment. Release is the misuse vector.
impact: Longer exposure window during incidents.
proposed_resolution: RR-TVR-OPS-002-r1.

title: Independence requirements sized for a large organisation produce nominal compliance at release-1 staffing
description: Three named people per control, mandatory rotation, a CISO reporting line and separate telemetry ownership assume a large staff; the source itself flags scale feasibility and small-scale compensation.
impact: Either unaffordable headcount or paper assignments that provide no real independence.
proposed_resolution: RR-OPS-004-r1; SPD-PLT-004; keep engine-enforced SoD and reconciliation outside the payment chain.

title: 46 rows deferred or conditional, mostly partners, embeds, white-label and non-default isolation profiles absent from release 1
description: Report 17 excludes distribution partners, white-label and embedded checkout. 31 rows are dispositioned defer and 15 conditional-on-operating-model. Building or testing them in R1 multiplies test matrices (three isolation profiles) and configuration.
impact: Avoided build/test effort; ~56 sponsor/partner settings not exposed in R1 [D: 245 total - 189 R1].
proposed_resolution: Tag as conditional; activate with the contract that requires them; isolation and security content applies in full when activated.

title: Traceability obligations applied uniformly instead of by risk class
description: Three scenarios per requirement, dual review of every control link and manual PR mapping are applied to presentation-only items as well as risk-bearing ones.
impact: ~195 h/yr [A] avoidable recurring; large one-time backlog.
proposed_resolution: RR-UNB-VAL-001-r1, RR-SOC2-007-r2.

title: Configuration surface in this slice: ~245 settings [A], ~189 in R1 scope [D], ~159 after removing the GOV-AUTH-001/UNB-RCN-PLT-005 overlap [D]
description: Largest items: notification catalog (~40), authority registry/matrix (~30 + 25, overlapping), step-up matrix (~18), entitlements (~15), per-partner tenancy policy (~10). Every parameter change requires independent approval (UNB-GOV-002).
impact: Onboarding effort and policy-change approvals (~80 h/yr [A]).
proposed_resolution: Default packs adopted by attestation, tighten-only (XID-ADV-010); RR-UNB-GOV-002-r1; single authority matrix.

title: Project-process and status statements carried as product requirements
description: Instructions to development agents, project telemetry, ID cross-reference maps and document-status notes are in the requirement baseline.
impact: Noise in traceability; each needs scenarios and control links under UNB-VAL-001 and RR-SOC2-007-r1.
proposed_resolution: Move to AGENTS.md / project governance; remove from baseline.

title: 20 REQ-X records (058-077) are scope statements, not testable requirements
description: REQ-X-058..077 say "Specify the full operating workflow in <spec>" or "Extend the one Unbound component monolith ... See the dedicated specification". The dedicated specs contain five generic capability bullets and a templated UX/contract/acceptance paragraph; none has acceptance criteria. The testable obligations were later written as UNB-RCN-*, UNB-XIN-* and RR-* records. Both layers are counted as requirements.
impact: Inflates the requirement count, duplicates traceability, and invites teams to build to bullets rather than to carriers; 8 of the 20 cover features excluded from release 1.
proposed_resolution: Reclassify REQ-X-058..077 as a non-normative capability index; each maps to its carriers (report section 2). Tests attach only to carriers. Deferred capabilities keep their index entry with status Deferred.

evidence: UNB-XIN-CLM-001 (default 90 days; outcomes upheld/reversed/modified/withdrawn);UNB-RCN-WF-018 (default 60 days; outcomes Upheld/Overturned/Modified/Referred);RCD-046 (appeal request window 60 days, response 30 days)
title: Reconsideration is defined three times with conflicting window and outcome set
description: UNB-RCN-ENT-016 creates the right, UNB-RCN-WF-018 sets 60 days and {Upheld, Overturned, Modified, Referred}, UNB-XIN-CLM-001 sets 90 days and {upheld, reversed, modified, withdrawn}. RCD-046 (decided-provisional) fixes 60 days. No conflict record exists in either conflicts.csv.
impact: Donors and charities could be told different deadlines by channel; reporting by outcome is inconsistent.
proposed_resolution: Keep UNB-XIN-CLM-001 as the only reconsideration record (case profile), with one window parameter defaulting to 60 days per RCD-046 and outcome set {Upheld, Reversed, Modified, Withdrawn, Referred}. Mark UNB-RCN-WF-018 and the reconsideration clause of UNB-RCN-ENT-016 consolidated.

title: TVR-CON-003 still states a donor receivable, contradicting adopted rules
description: TVR-CON-003 says a reversed contribution that funded disbursements "creates a donor receivable". RR-REQ-X-009-r1 and RR-TVR-CON-001-r1 say it MUST NOT presume a receivable unless counsel confirms an enforceable claim; shortfall posts as sponsor operating loss (XID-BNK-006).
impact: An implementer reading the TVR register would post a receivable and could pursue donors for a gift they reversed.
proposed_resolution: Annotate TVR-CON-003 as superseded by RR-REQ-X-009-r1/RR-TVR-CON-001-r1; keep the "no silent negative fund" invariant inside RR-REQ-X-009-r1.

title: Nine reconciliation records are pointers or restatements of refinements
description: UNB-RCN-ENT-004 restates RR-UNB-SUCC-008-r1 step 2; ENT-005/010/012/014 only say "per RR-..."; ENT-007 points to RR-UNB-WF-014-r1 plus one inbound clause; WF-011 duplicates UNB-XIN-TRS-004 restoration; WF-012 adds one blocked command to ProtectiveHold; WF-013 restates RCD-041 within RR-UNB-ADV-001-r1.
impact: Each pointer doubles test and trace work and can drift from its target.
proposed_resolution: Merge the unique clauses (inbound transfer classification; standing debits under ProtectiveHold) into the survivors and mark the pointers consolidated.

title: Landscape conversion waves 01/02 are outcome indexes, hypotheses and research tasks
description: Of 68 wave records in this slice, LS-001..017 restate outcomes O-01..O-18, HYP-001..010 are hypotheses (5 already resolved into requirements), COM-001..004 and GAP-001..009 are business-model and evidence tasks, WF-001..024 restate workflows now specified by refinements. Only UNB-CAP-002, UNB-CAP-003 and UNB-WF-024 carry unique normative content.
impact: Requirement count and gate denominators include ~68 records with no system behaviour.
proposed_resolution: Keep the waves as a trace index; move GAP-001..009, COM-001 and open hypotheses to an evidence backlog with owners; count only carriers in the requirements gate (UNB-RCN-ENT-001).

title: Annual affiliation attestation for every advisory holder is calendar-driven friction
description: CRM-002 requires annual attestation of affiliations by every advisory-privilege holder. Capturing affiliations is a needed input to 4967/4958 screening (TVCTL-14), but the annual calendar is a convention; report 09 cross-cutting conclusion 2 replaces calendar work with change-driven work.
impact: ~1.3 interactions per account per year [A: 1.3 holders per fund] and ~217 staff hours per 10k accounts chasing non-responders [A].
proposed_resolution: Event-driven update plus a prefilled one-step confirmation in the next authenticated session after 12 months; separate outreach only when a recommendation is pending and the holder has been absent for 12 months.

title: Monthly statement notification and optional mail by default are conventions
description: REQ-X-032 generates monthly statements by default with email notification and optional physical mail. Report 09 line 33 already classifies statement cadence as sponsor policy and lists monthly-by-default as an inherited step. Statements are not statutory; contribution acknowledgments are.
impact: Up to 12 notifications per account per year [A] and print/mail cost where mail is chosen.
proposed_resolution: RR-REQ-X-032-r1: generate and publish each period automatically; notify per preference (proposed default quarterly digest plus correction alerts); paper only on request or without e-delivery consent.

title: No ask-once rule for establishment intake
description: UNB-XIN-CLM-003 forbids re-requesting Fresh facts in InformationRequests, but ADM-002 intake has no equivalent; a donor opening a second fund or an advisor joining another fund can be asked again for identity and contact data held for the same PartyId. ADM-014 keeps agreement re-acceptance undefined.
impact: Duplicate data entry (UNB-CAP-003 failure mechanism); avoidable follow-ups ~25 h per 10k accounts [A].
proposed_resolution: RR-ADM-002-r1 (prefill and confirm; click-accept agreement; no proofing for view-only participants).

title: Routine fund acceptance and activation are not written as deterministic
description: ADM-003 separates drafted, accepted, created and activated states but leaves acceptance as a human act; report 09 line 22 proposes "open on policy match" and RCD-005 provides the delegation pattern, but no requirement carries it.
impact: ~167 staff hours per 10k accounts per year [D: 1,000 new funds x 10 min, both assumptions].
proposed_resolution: RR-ADM-003-r1 with the same authority-flag switch as RCD-005 (AcceptRecommended batch until the board delegates).

evidence: unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:392;unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:407 (REQ-X-085 heading; not in inventory.csv);unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:470-482;unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/19-questions/PROPOSED-CANONICAL-REQUIREMENTS-AND-ACCEPTANCE-2026-11-22.md:499-517 (REQ-X-086..089 headings; not in inventory.csv)
title: Exception management and AI assistance are each defined several times
description: REQ-X-041 has a second definition renumbered REQ-X-085; REQ-X-053/054/055 overlap with renumbered REQ-X-086..089; REQ-X-024 notes duplicate the case/subject timeline. UNB-XIN-SVC-001/002 already make exceptions a case kind.
impact: Multiple components with the same purpose; inconsistent authority boundaries for AI.
proposed_resolution: Survivors: UNB-XIN-SVC-002 (exceptions), REQ-X-053 (AI assistance, R1 explanation-only), RR-REQ-X-048-r2 (work items).

title: The only recurring-obligation register is deferred with the high-volume-low-balance model
description: UNB-XIN-ADV-001 is the single record that classifies every recurring per-account obligation by legal basis (statutory, fiduciary, contractual, sponsor policy, risk control, convention). It was deferred because DigitalMinimal is not an R1 model, which also defers the inventory.
impact: No standing mechanism shows which per-account work and donor interactions are convention-driven.
proposed_resolution: Split: register (inventory with interactions per account-year) applies in R1 for all classes; DigitalMinimal budget enforcement stays deferred.

title: Technology choices embedded in requirements
description: REQ-X-033 names Typst and ADM-036 names WASM-first Forma; REQ-X-012 and RCD-027 put technology selection behind ADRs.
impact: A rendering or UI technology change would appear as a requirement change.
proposed_resolution: Move technology choices to ADRs; keep outcomes (reproducible bytes, accessibility).

title: Continued-holding re-review every 12 months is calendar work
description: UNB-RCN-WF-030 re-reviews every fund held after dormancy outreach every 12 months. Under the change-driven principle, a re-review is useful only when something changes (activity, contact restored, balance threshold, program change).
impact: ~50 staff hours per 10k accounts per year [A]; little decision value.
proposed_resolution: Event-driven re-review plus automated reconfirmation outreach; human only at disposition.

title: Evidence tasks have no owner or due date
description: Shadow replay (GAP-001) is the measurement that would replace the economic model's assumed e and m, which drive the per-account exception cost; it sits in a requirement list with no owner.
impact: Every hour estimate in this register stays [A] until it runs.
proposed_resolution: Evidence backlog with owner, due date and the decision each item unblocks.

title: Agreement re-acceptance on every terms change is undefined
description: ADM-014 requires versioned, signed acknowledgments but does not say which changes need re-acceptance; the safe default in practice is re-acceptance for all, which generates donor prompts and staff chasing.
impact: ~0.5 prompts per account per year and ~83 staff hours per 10k [A] if terms change yearly.
proposed_resolution: Counsel defines material changes; non-material changes are notice-only; wet signatures are never required.

title: The '6–8 person' floor is an unvalidated structure-dependent assumption, not a derivation
description: The figures 6–8 (TVA-022), 8–10 (org model), 8 (conventional comparator floor in the baseline model) and ~20/21 (AI-native role floors incl. 4 engineers and 4 agent owners) measure different things: authority coverage, workload and platform build. The SoD pair graph is bipartite, so pure SoD needs 2 people (org §4:85). With per-item SoD and cross-training, the derived payment-chain authority floor is 4 named holders for single-absence cover or 5 for double absence [D], held by 2–4 sponsor FTE at 1k accounts when platform, reconciliation review, assurance, counsel and tax are purchased [D from A inputs].
impact: Generic floors over-staff small sponsors (S1) or under-protect SoD in December.
proposed_resolution: RR-UNB-ECO-003-r1 (three-term floor) and UNB-SMP-ORG-002 (coverage roster).

title: TVR-OPS-004 (rota/on-call) is referenced but never defined

title: Several revenue models reward asset retention, delayed or withheld grants, or preservation of manual work

proposed_resolution: Report exposure and containment by kind (ECO-016 counter-metric set).

title: Below ~10k accounts every operating model costs $580-870 (10k) to ~$4,600 (1k) per account
description: About 21 fixed FTE plus queue floors dominate; consistent with the 09 model's finding that a 1k-account AI-native sponsor costs more than a conventional one.

Evidence MUST record one AffirmationEvidence item per representation under UNB-RCN-GRT-010. description: RR-ADM-042-r1 defines contact rates, repeat contacts, deflection and resolution time. ADM-047 (abandonment) and INT-020 (effort, errors, abandonment) still have no formulas. Nothing measures unnecessary data entry or effort per journey.
impact: Friction reduction claims in this report cannot be verified after launch.
proposed_resolution: RR-ADM-042-r2 adds the definitions in report section 'Friction metrics'.

Treating the donor checkbox as the legal requirement could lead to unnecessary re-affirmation of control, for example per contribution.

proposed_resolution: Disposition 'eliminate' (platform-owned) in config-items.jsonl. UNB-SMP-CFG-003 forbids exposing platform-owned items to sponsors.

proposed_resolution: Apply one suppression rule to every cross-sponsor metric in the registry (part of RR-REQ-X-043-r1). Threshold: SPD-DSH-002.

title: No documented Unbound advantage survives a well-funded competitor with the same technology
description: Every differentiator in the requirement set (journal-authoritative ledger, contract-first API, AI flag-only controls, measured SLOs, WCAG conformance, full-history export, default policy packs) is technology, policy or practice that a funded vendor can copy in months. The only structural candidate — not being paid on assets or through affiliates — holds against incumbents only.
impact: Business cases that assume a moat from the architecture would overstate durable margin; competitive position would depend on execution speed, assured operating track record, distribution and network scale, none of which Unbound holds.
proposed_resolution: State in strategy documents that Unbound's advantages are execution-dependent; prioritise measurable operating evidence (SOC 2 Type II period, measured SLOs, cost per grant) over feature breadth; see SPD-CMP-001.

title: Small-balance market expansion is weakly supported and faces a tax headwind
description: OBBBA excludes DAF gifts from the new nonitemizer deduction (X02: $1,500 DAF gift by a nonitemizer yields $0 deduction vs $1,500 direct). Fidelity and Schwab removed minimums in 2020 and Daffy is free under $100, so access already exists. 79.5% of reported accounts are processor accounts holding 0.9% of assets. Modelled break-even at 0.60% is ~$40.7k–$45.3k [D from illustrative S].
impact: A low-balance strategy would mostly redistribute share from processors and digital challengers rather than expand the market, at negative unit margin until metered cost-to-serve is far below modelled figures.
proposed_resolution: Keep high-volume/low-balance out of R1 (consistent with XID-ADV-002); require any future low-balance case to show metered cost below the fee floor and a donor benefit that survives the nonitemizer exclusion.

title: Competitive 'uniqueness' claims rest on public-page absence
description: Report 05 classifies export (CAP-17) as a differentiator because 'no top-10 sponsor documents one', but the underlying census marks ND = not found on public pages, and logged-in features were not checked. Daffy already offers CSV export and Greater Washington CF a CSV export. Similar caution applies to API and AI capabilities at Fidelity, Vanguard, NPT and Ren.
impact: External messaging or prioritisation built on 'only provider' claims could be false and misleading.
proposed_resolution: Treat CAP-17/CAP-16/CAP-24 as 'differentiation relative to public documentation only'; require logged-in verification before any external claim (SPD-CMP-004).

title: The best-evidenced addressable gap (community foundations) is the segment R1 cannot serve
description: CFs show the highest DAF cost (127–177 bps standard; tail CF DAF admin plausibly $1.2k–$4.1k per account [I]) and active vendor switching, but ~43% of mapped CF assets sit behind portal-only front ends with external ledgers, and DAFs are only 17.7% of a tail CF's assets. R1 assumes Unbound is book of record for every function and defers Shadow-book support (XID-ADV-003); endowment/designated-fund administration is not in scope.
impact: Unbound would compete against Foundant (361 CFs) without the multi-fund-type and external-GL capabilities CFs need; the CF opportunity is share redistribution requiring scope R1 excludes.
proposed_resolution: Decide the primary target segment (SPD-CMP-001) before release-1 scope is approved; if CFs, re-open XID-ADV-003 and scope non-DAF fund types.

title: Scale economies favour incumbents on cost per grant
description: Observed cost per grant is ~$55 (DAFgiving360), ~$68 (Fidelity), ~$134 (Vanguard) [S]; Unbound's own model puts its high case at ~$96 per grant and per-account cost only approaching the Fidelity-derived frontier. Cost elasticity to scale is 0.41 for nationals.
impact: A cost-leadership claim against the large nationals is not supported; any cost advantage is plausible only against high-cost segments (CFs, single-issue sponsors).
proposed_resolution: Benchmark Unbound's six R1 metrics (XID-ADV-011) against the published per-grant figures once measured; do not claim cost leadership against nationals.

title: Charity-side payment networks are a competitor advantage a single-sponsor platform cannot match
description: Ren onboards a charity's ACH once for all Ren-administered DAFs; Chariot holds claimed nonprofit accounts across Daffy, TIFIN Give, Charityvest and seven CFs; PayPal Grant Payments serves NPT and Vanguard. R1 pays by ACH by default with the sponsor as Originator, which means per-sponsor charity bank-detail collection and verification.
impact: Higher charity onboarding friction and destination-verification cost than networked rails; report 05 already recommends partnering a rail.
proposed_resolution: Decide rail strategy explicitly (SPD-CMP-003); prefer a networked rail adapter for R1 where contract terms permit.

title: Donor-side AI availability lags competitors while control design leads on paper
description: Daffy's live MCP exposes make_donation without documented limits; TIFIN's Louise executes donor requests with 8 of 10 controls undocumented; Chariot and Endaoment have MCP/CLI surfaces. Several sponsor terms (NCF, Vanguard, NPT) bar credential sharing or AI use. Unbound's controlled design is unshipped.
impact: Unbound can claim safer agent access only once implemented; until then competitors are superior on availability.
proposed_resolution: Position AI as 'controlled agent access' (scoped OAuth, step-up, actor identity) and measure it; do not compete on breadth of autonomous actions.

title: Published service levels and accessibility conformance are a cheap, credible but replicable differentiator
description: 0 of 13 readable top-20 sponsors claim a WCAG level; none publishes a quantified response time or turnaround distribution. Unbound designs SLOs and a WCAG 2.2 AA gate but no requirement found here obliges sponsors or the platform to publish them to donors and charities.
impact: Low cost to gain trust signals; easily copied, so value is first-mover and reputational only.
proposed_resolution: Owner decision SPD-CMP-002 on publishing conformance and measured SLOs; if adopted, refine UNB-XIN-SAS-008 rather than add a requirement.

title: The $258 per-account reference figure has no source; it is the midpoint of an illustrative range
description: The mission direction uses ~$258/account as the starting rung. No document in unbound or the landscape synthesis states $258. The sources state $244-$272 fully allocated, illustrative [S]; (244+272)/2 = 258 [D]. The economic model itself uses $272 at 100k accounts. Both endpoints are assumption-driven model outputs, not observations.
impact: A derived midpoint presented as a reference value becomes false precision (Clarity admissibility, rules.md:56) and anchors every downstream rung.
proposed_resolution: Consolidated into SPF-ECN-001 (duplicate $258 finding; SPF-ADV-017). Cite the range $244-$272 [S, illustrative] and label any single value [D] with its derivation; never present it as a measured baseline.

title: The $10 per-account target is below single documented cost components and is unfalsifiable without a cost layer and scale
description: Custody alone is $14.40/account in Unbound's own example [S]; low-case exception labour is $9/account [S]. At 100k accounts, $10 x 100k = $1.0m [D], which funds 6.1-8.0 loaded FTE at $124.5k-$165k [S] with zero technology, custody, payment, AI, counsel or audit cost [D]. Break-even balances at an assumed 0.60% fee: $1,667 ($10), $4,167 ($25), $8,333 ($50), $16,667 ($100), $43,000 ($258) [D]. As written the ladder does not say whether it is fully allocated or marginal, sponsor or fund-borne, or at what scale.
impact: Plans, pricing or investor models built on $10 fully allocated would rest on a figure contradicted by the model's own components; small-balance viability could be wrongly asserted or wrongly rejected.
proposed_resolution: Restate each rung as a hypothesis with (a) cost layer: marginal vs fully allocated; (b) bearer: sponsor, fund, platform; (c) scale: account count; (d) servicing class. Treat $10 as a marginal-cost hypothesis for a DigitalMinimal class with fund-borne custody. Decision SPD-CLR-001.

title: The 6-8 staffing floor is mis-cited and conflicts with four other documented floors; "below the floor" is undefined
description: Discovery reports 10, 11 and 14 cite "6-8 (TVC-018)". TVC-018 records "~20 at any scale" vs "8-10" and notes they may measure different things. The organization model corrects the SoD minimum to 2 (bipartite graph) and preserves an unresolved ~10+ for two-deep holiday coverage of the payment chain. The landscape synthesis calls 6-8 "an unvalidated assumption, not an industry minimum".
impact: R8 (staffing below the floor) cannot be evaluated or falsified; staffing plans may under-provide SoD coverage on worst days.
proposed_resolution: Correct the citation in reports 10/11/14 (owner action; this group does not edit them). Replace headcount floors with a roster-derived minimum by role and day (UNB-SMP-CLR-001). Decision SPD-CLR-002.

title: Provisional legal/accounting positions are at risk of Assumption Drift once adopted into domain files
description: 41 decisions were made by the integrator (an AI agent) at the owner's direction and are not legal or accounting opinions. 46 records were adopted into domain files as binding for design. Verification of a subset changed at least four positions; an adversarial spot check found 2 of 11 legal claims wrong. Only five decisions are feature-gated on opinions. If each of 41 decisions independently had a 5% chance of reversal, P(all stand) = 12%; at 10%, 1.3% [D] -- and errors are likely correlated (one model family, shared sources).
impact: Built behaviour may issue acknowledgments, journals or statements under positions later overturned; reversal cost grows with each downstream record.
proposed_resolution: Machine-enforce provisional status: no production activation of behaviour whose basis is unconfirmed (UNB-SMP-CLR-002); assign each decision a dated human owner; order confirmations by downstream dependency and irreversibility (SPD-CLR-003).
decision_owner: General counsel + external CPA + product owner

title: The detective control that makes automatic approval auditable has an unbudgeted labour cost
description: Decision-quality sampling (UNB-XIN-CLM-005) must report error rate with a confidence interval. To estimate a 1% error rate within +/-0.5 pp at 95% needs n = 1.96^2 x 0.01 x 0.99 / 0.005^2 = 1,521 reviews per period [D]; at 10 minutes per review [A] that is ~254 hours/month, ~1.9 FTE at 1,600 h/yr [D]. At +/-1 pp, 381 reviews, ~0.5 FTE [D]. None of the economics documents includes this cost.
impact: Minimum-touch savings are overstated and R8 staffing understated by roughly 0.5-2 FTE; or sampling is under-sized and automated approval becomes unauditable.
proposed_resolution: Size the sampling plan explicitly (risk-stratified, sequential sampling to reduce n), include it in the cost case and the roster; benchmark TB-09.

title: Clarity and EDF describe Clarity's role differently; neither is a gate
description: Clarity says it is not primarily a decision framework and governs reasoning depth; EDF says Clarity answers "What should we do?" and evaluates decisions. The reconciliation rules that both are vocabulary, not gates.
impact: Readers may treat Clarity results here as approvals.
proposed_resolution: State in every consumer that Clarity results are reasoning maps and EDF sufficiency is action-relative; no requirement is approved by either.

title: Neither method nor the stakeholder passes constitute independent validation
description: Clarity's held-out benchmark found current Clarity no more accurate than no method and less useful; EDF's incremental value is unsupported; all passes here and in the discovery package are one model family.
impact: Over-reading this evaluation as validation would add Confidence Debt.
proposed_resolution: Put the falsifiers and counter-arguments in front of real counsel, CPA, auditor, compliance and sponsor-board holders; treat this report as a question list.

title: Minimum-touch economics depend on Tier-1 policy approval, which is gated on an unanswered counsel question
description: Tier-1 deterministic board-delegated approval is "permitted only where OD-01 is validated for that sponsor"; validation still required: RCD-005 counsel Q1 plus a sponsor board resolution. The STP rate assumed by R1 and the staffing in R8 presuppose Tier 1.
impact: A negative or narrow counsel answer collapses the STP assumption and raises e towards 100% of grants for human approval.
proposed_resolution: Obtain counsel Q1 before sizing staff on STP; model a no-Tier-1 fallback (SPD-CLR-004).

title: Burden externalization is unmeasured in release 1
description: Minimum-touch, self-service, charity data maintenance and outsourced specialists move work. The landscape research agenda asks to "quantify displaced rather than eliminated work". In R1 only counter-metrics would see displaced work, and the counter-metric floors are deferred.
impact: Cost per account could fall while donor, charity and advisor effort rises, violating the mission principle that moved work is not elimination.
proposed_resolution: Add a displaced-work measure (donor/charity/advisor task minutes and contacts per account) to the R1 six-metric catalog as a counter-metric.

title: Release 1 pursues cost reduction without the counter-metric halt rule designed to stop control erosion
description: Report 17 defers "the improvement loop and its floors" (ECO-015/016) while R1 measures six cost metrics "each with its counter-metric". Without the floor-breach halt (ECO-016), nothing stops a cost gain that comes from reduced detection -- the failure ECO-016 AC-2 exists to catch (Goodhart).
impact: Automation or staffing reductions in R1 could erode controls undetected.
proposed_resolution: Carry only the ECO-016 halt rule (floor breach halts the initiative and blocks crediting the saving) into R1, without the rest of the loop. Proposed revised statement for UNB-XIN-ECO-016 scope: "In release 1, the floors for control effectiveness (1) and compliance (2) MUST apply to any automation enablement or staffing change; other floors deferred."

title: EDF was applied outside its diagnostic scope by declared adaptation
description: EDF diagnoses how an outcome was produced; the recommendations are prospective. The Outcome field was restricted to documented facts motivating each recommendation and the predicted outcome was recorded separately as a hypothesis. Control-point ranking is heuristic (HY-EDF-004 suggestive) and confidence is qualitative.
impact: Treating EDF control-point rankings as validated priorities would overstate them.
proposed_resolution: Use rankings as ordering hypotheses for discussion; re-run EDF on real incidents after launch, where it is in scope.

title: The highest-leverage control points for per-account cost are cost-layer separation, per-account obligations and exception rate -- not headcount
description: EDF origin network for small-account cost: asset-fee revenue, fixed/step-fixed allocations, per-account recurring obligations, custody/payment unit costs, and conflated denominators. Exception labour is linear in e and m (elasticity 1). Ranking: cost-layer separation first (definitional, cheap, enables measurement), then per-account obligation budget (UNB-XIN-ADV-001), then pricing, then exception rate.
impact: Targeting headcount first (R8) attacks a lower-leverage, lower-controllability control point.
proposed_resolution: Sequence economics work: layer separation and balance-band measurement in R1, obligation budget before any small-balance model, staffing last.

title: Default packs, the shared registry and shared AI create common-mode failure paths across sponsors
description: Report 12 lists "a correlated misconfiguration of a policy pack shared across sponsors" as a residual risk no architecture removes. Existing simulation requirements (UNB-RULE-019, UNB-GEX-024, REQ-X-045) are per-rule and per-sponsor; none requires cross-sponsor evaluation or staged rollout of a shared pack version. "Sponsors may only tighten" is undefined for non-ordinal parameters.
impact: One pack defect can affect every adopting sponsor at the same effective date.
proposed_resolution: Refine UNB-RULE-019 (RR-UNB-RULE-019-r1): cross-sponsor shadow evaluation, staged rollout, rollback, per-parameter ordering or enumerated alternatives. Decision SPD-EDF-001.

title: Unobserved origin: feed specifications underpin P0 controls that minimum-touch makes the only line of defence
description: Idempotency keys, daily debit matching and positive pay depend on bank/custodian specifications nobody has obtained. Under minimum-touch, no human is positioned to notice a duplicate or dropped correction.
impact: Silent duplicates or missed corrections in automated matching.
proposed_resolution: Make feed conformance (TB-12) a precondition for enabling automated matching, not only for go-live.

title: Registry-unavailability behaviour is neither tested nor specified as an acceptance criterion
description: XIF-ADV-007 proposed adding an acceptance criterion to UNB-XIN-EVA-011 for registry unavailability (fail closed). EVA-011 still has only AC-1 and AC-2. The benchmark placed the hold registry in the same database, so cross-database release latency and outage behaviour are unmeasured.
impact: The single fail-closed gate for every sponsor's releases has no specified or tested failure behaviour.
proposed_resolution: Proposed revised statement for UNB-XIN-EVA-011 (add AC-3): "Given the hold registry is unreachable or returns a version older than the release command's read; when release or dispatch is attempted; then the item is not released, it is marked HeldRegistryUnavailable, no AI or human path bypasses the check, and items resume automatically after a fresh version read." For R1, co-locate (SPD-ARX-001). Benchmark TB-02.

title: With one release-1 sponsor, several multi-tenant elements are unnecessary in R1
description: A separate platform registry database, three isolation profiles, per-partner schema templating (DG-11) and migration fan-out tooling serve multi-sponsor operation that R1 excludes.
impact: Building them in R1 adds operational surface for a small team with no R1 beneficiary.
proposed_resolution: Keep logical seams (tenant envelope, routing per UNB-TEN-019, registry as its own schema and role with the versioned contract); defer physical separation to the second sponsor.

title: The protective emergency plane second durable store is not justified for a minimum-touch R1
description: REQ-X-047 adds a second durable store outside the monolith; RCF-ARC-004 asks for explicit justification. With a small team, a second store adds a recovery path to rehearse and operate. No RTO evidence shows the primary path insufficient.
impact: Operational complexity without demonstrated necessity.
proposed_resolution: Defer until TB-07 shows the managed primary cannot meet declared RTO/RPO (SPD-ARX-002).

title: Automation fallbacks assume human capacity that a minimum-touch organization does not have
description: At the Unbound December volume of 8,000 grants/day [S], routing suspended automation to human review needs ~1,333 reviewer-hours/day at 10 min/grant or ~267 at 2 min [D] -- tens to hundreds of reviewers. Only custodian outages have a defined degraded mode (UNB-CUST-022); kill switches stop new commands (UNB-XIN-SAS-002) but no requirement defines capacity-aware fallback for automated decision paths.
impact: Suspension in December either breaches SLAs massively or invites unsafe auto-release by age.
proposed_resolution: New requirement UNB-SMP-ARX-001: declared fallback per automated path, hold-and-notify default, backlog projection against roster, prohibition of release by age. Benchmark TB-10.

title: Benchmark coverage gaps that matter more under minimum-touch
description: Report 18 limits: 60-second runs, synthetic uniform data, fast local fsync, no reporting or snapshot sealing, registry co-located, no recovery. Minimum-touch increases reliance on unattended long-running behaviour (vacuum, timers, recovery).
impact: Production surprises in exactly the paths no human watches.
proposed_resolution: Run TB-01..TB-04 and TB-07 before production; keep ADR falsification criteria as reconsideration criteria.

title: The release-1 fallback for missing bank specifications is a recurring manual task incompatible with minimum-touch staffing
description: Report 17 lists "Manual daily reconciliation, which is costly" as the fallback if the bank partner's ACH and statement-file specification is not obtained.
impact: Invoking the fallback silently invalidates R1 and R8 assumptions.
proposed_resolution: Treat the bank specification as a hard dependency for the minimum-touch operating model, or cost the manual fallback into the roster (UNB-SMP-CLR-001).

title: Per-record retention disposition review is a recurring human task that grows with volume
description: RR-REQ-X-036-r1 requires that expiry create a disposition review task and forbids automatic deletion. At hundreds of millions of rows per year (fee accruals alone ~110m rows/yr at 100k accounts, report 12) per-record tasks are infeasible.
impact: Either disposition never happens (over-retention of personal data) or reviews are rubber-stamped.
proposed_resolution: Proposed revised statement: "Expiry MUST create one disposition review per (retention class, sponsor, expiry period) batch, listing counts and any records under legal hold; an authorized reviewer approves or defers the batch; deletion MUST NOT occur without that approval; records under legal hold are excluded automatically."

title: Shared-platform economics (OM3-OM5) pool all exception, complex-gift, service and ops staff at the platform operator and size them once for the whole book.
description: The model's platform operating models (OM3, OM4, OM5) place every queue role - including the exception-grant decider (A4), gift-acceptance authority and treasury exception approver - on the platform operator and staff them as one pool across 20-200 sponsors. The organisation pass rejects exactly this (SPR-ORG-004) and recommends that vendor staff stay below A3 unless individually appointed by each sponsor's board (SPD-ORG-002; UNB-XIN-CLM-008). The sponsor's exclusive legal control (IRC 4966(d)(2)) requires that the person exercising discretion on a sponsor's grant be that sponsor's authorised principal. The model contains no per-sponsor authority floor in platform models. Executed variant V1 (adds 2.5 FTE x $165k [A, ops S1 floor] per sponsor): OM3@100k P50 $192 -> $238 [D]; OM3@1M $125 -> $174 [D]; OM4@1M $29 -> $40 [D]; OM5@5M $14 -> $18 [D]. At 100k accounts the shared platform (OM3, 20 sponsors) becomes dearer than the lean self-operated sponsor (OM2 P50 $180).
impact: The headline conclusion that a shared platform reaches $100-$25 per account rests partly on pooling legal authority that the same mission says cannot be pooled. Either the economics or the governance position is wrong.
proposed_resolution: Restate OM3-OM5 with an explicit per-sponsor authority floor (or with board-appointed shared deciders under SPD-ADV-001) and re-run the targets table; until then mark OM3-OM5 results as conditional on SPD-ADV-001. Do not adopt SPD-ECN-001 bands before this.

SPD-ECN-001 proposes 'Standard <= $200 P50 at 100k' and 'DigitalMinimal <= $30 P50 at 1M'; both fail under V5. $258 remains reachable by OM2 at 100k and OM3 at 1M; $100 is not reachable at P50 by any variant; $50 only by OM5 at >=1M.

title: More than half of the lean-model saving comes from one fragile lever (complex-gift hours 12 -> 2) that is paired with a bearer shift to donor funds.
description: Adding OM2 levers one at a time to OM1@100k (deterministic, modal): complex_hours 12->2 saves $58.65 of the $103.03 OM1->OM2 saving (57%) [D]; outsourcing complex assets moves $16.98 per account to funds as vendor fees [D]. The ops pass itself calls the 2-hour residual 'the single most fragile assumption' (SPF-ORG-006). Gift acceptance remains an A4 sponsor decision, so a 2-hour residual includes sponsor authority time that a vendor cannot absorb.

description: The model applies advisor-channel CAC ($400 [A], 15% new per year) to workplace and small-balance books and books it to the employer. title: Sanctions false-positive dispositions are reused with no sponsor (legal-entity) scope.
description: RR-UNB-EXT-004-r2 reuses a human false-positive disposition for all later screenings of the same subject against the same list-entry version. On a shared platform this lets one sponsor's officer clear a potential match for every sponsor. Each sponsor bears its own OFAC strict liability and its own SoD (sanctions decider is a named sponsor role, ORG-R07). SPD-GRT-003 asks only about maximum age and triggers.
impact: Cross-sponsor reliance on another legal entity's sanctions determination without counsel approval; correlated error across sponsors.
proposed_resolution: Scope reuse to the sponsor legal entity that made the disposition unless counsel approves cross-sponsor reliance (SPD-ADV-002); record the relying sponsor's reliance event.

title: Platform-authored legal-change policy packs would change a sponsor's approval policy by silence.
description: SPD-CFG-001 recommends that legal-change packs auto-apply after 30 days unless a sponsor objects. A pack can loosen as well as tighten (override directions in UNB-SMP-CFG-002), and the platform's classification of a change as 'legal' is itself a legal interpretation. Sponsor exclusive legal control and SPD-CFG-003 ('sponsor retains exclusive legal control') require an affirmative sponsor act for any change that relaxes a control. Auto-apply also propagates one drafting error to every sponsor at once.
impact: Policy changes without the sponsor's affirmative act; common-mode error.
proposed_resolution: Auto-apply only changes that are strictly tightening under the deterministic comparator AND have passed per-sponsor shadow evaluation (RR-UNB-RULE-019-r1) AND rest on confirmed decisions (UNB-SMP-CLR-002); everything else needs re-attestation. See SPR-ADV-001.

Several duplicate or are not release-1 needs.

proposed_resolution: Cut 13 gap requirements to 7 (merge CLR-001 into ORG-002, ECN-001 into ECN-003, CFG-003 into CFG-002; fold ECN-002 into UNB-XIN-ECO-017 as an AC; defer DSH-001; make CXP-001 a design-review artefact); reclassify the three ECO model refinements as analysis governance; cut kept metrics to the XID-ADV-011 six plus counter-metrics and control monitors; merge 6 duplicate decisions and move ~8 commercial/strategy decisions to a backlog.

title: The customer pass keeps 70 metrics while the adopted release-1 position is a six-metric economics catalog.
description: 14 of 84 metrics are dropped; 70 are kept across 14 audiences. The register pass itself folds lifecycle analytics into the six-metric catalog (ADM-047 reasoning). Many kept metrics are operational queue views that need no registry entry.
impact: Metric maintenance and dashboard surface far above decision needs.
proposed_resolution: R1: XID-ADV-011 six metrics + their counter-metrics + SPD-DSH-001 executive set + control monitors required by law or controls; everything else is a queue view, not a registered metric.

title: Deferring SOC reports moves assurance cost to the sponsor's auditor, and the model under-ranges assurance cost for multi-sponsor platforms.
description: SPD-PLT-001 defers SOC system descriptions until a second user entity. If Unbound keeps the sponsor's DAF program ledger and is operated by a separate operator entity, the sponsor's financial-statement auditor must test those IT general controls directly (unverified - general knowledge), a cost borne by the sponsor and absent from the model. OM3-OM5 serve 10-200 sponsors and would need a SOC 1 Type II (and likely SOC 2) from year one; audit_base is fixed at $120k with no Monte Carlo range.
impact: Hidden cost displaced to the sponsor; platform cost floor slightly understated.
proposed_resolution: Record the displaced audit cost in the bearer map; give audit/assurance a range and a per-platform SOC line for OM3-OM5; keep SPD-PLT-001 for the single-sponsor R1 only if the operator and sponsor are the same entity or the auditor confirms direct testing is acceptable.

title: Two eliminated customer steps remove fraud controls without a compensating risk trigger.
description: SPX-027 removes step-up for grant recommendations of any size; SPX-003 removes source-of-funds questions except for complex assets. An account takeover can then recommend large grants to a recipient the attacker controls (a sham or complicit charity); large cash contributions from unknown sources are unscreened. Payee changes keep step-up, but recommendation of a new recipient does not.
impact: Account-takeover and laundering exposure moved from friction to loss.
proposed_resolution: Keep both steps risk-triggered (new device + new recipient + amount above band; contribution above a band or unusual pattern) rather than eliminated.

title: Growth shocks are handled by acknowledgment rather than prevented.
description: UNB-SMP-ECN-002 lets an approver acknowledge a forecast SLA collapse and proceed. The model shows migration at 100k drops SLA to 22% with 67,488 items unresolved 60 days after year end. Prevention is phasing intake to capacity.
impact: Customer harm in the largest modelled failure mode is accepted by signature.
proposed_resolution: Revise ECN-002: default to phased intake (waves sized so forecast SLA stays above floor); proceed above capacity only with pre-contracted surge (SPD-ECN-004) in place.

title: The recommended entry segment is the one the economics model says is most expensive to serve.
description: SPD-CMP-001 treats community-foundation/independent-sponsor administration as the leading entry hypothesis. Accounts per sponsor is the #1 cost driver in every platform model; at 1,000 accounts per sponsor OM3@1M costs ~$166 (modal) vs $88 at 5,000. Adding a per-sponsor authority floor (SPF-ADV-001) makes small sponsors costlier still. The typical DAF count of a community foundation is not sourced in the mission (unverified).
impact: Strategy and economics point in opposite directions; a competitor with larger sponsors keeps the cost advantage.
proposed_resolution: Test the entry hypothesis with sponsor-size distribution data before committing; price a per-sponsor component (SPD-ECN-003) and shared-service authority models (SPD-ADV-001) explicitly.

evidence: unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-24-simplification-economics/data/roles.jsonl (all 24 roles can_be_fractional=Y; ORG-R16/R17 outsourceable, operator-side in S1)
title: In the recommended solo-sponsor structure the platform operator can both configure the AI and sign off its model risk.
description: S1 places AI configuration owner (ORG-R16) operator-side and allows model-risk sign-off (ORG-R17) to be outsourced; nothing prevents the same operator from holding both. The operator's commercial interest (per-account pricing) differs from the sponsor's. Every role is fractional, so a few part-time individuals may hold many A4 roles across sponsors.
impact: Conflict of interest and concentration of authority.
proposed_resolution: Require ORG-R17 to be independent of the operator; cap A4 roles per individual and per sponsor count (SPD-ADV-001).

title: AI-assisted QA and after-the-fact sampling lack a check on cases where AI and the original outcome agree.
description: Where humans adjudicate only disagreements, correlated errors (same model family drafting and scoring) are never reviewed. UNB-XIN-CLM-005 sampling has no stated sample size or detection target, and its labour is unbudgeted (SPF-CLR-005).
impact: The only detective control behind straight-through approval may detect nothing.
proposed_resolution: Require a random human-reviewed share of AI-agreeing cases and a sample size per stratum that detects a stated error rate at stated confidence; budget the hours.

Both components are illustrative and differ in scope (one includes ~$60 acquisition and ~$15 fund-borne custody).

proposed_resolution: Label the midpoint explanation [H] and keep a single finding (SPF-ECN-001).
